Isn't it already done, that a server's average ping and response latency is tested by other devices regularly? Given these, we can map a packet's path through the network and compare the length of the path it took to the average response rate of other packets at that time. With this kind of attention, it's possible to know if - for example - an ATT network device held on to your packet for X seconds before passing it on, which was unusual because all other identical network packets were passed through that connection in half that time.

The SPAM Filter sits in front of the mail server and looks at all the messages before it forwards them to your mailbox. It can block on the address, domain, or a string of text in the email. You don't have to have a dedicated box for spam filtering another popular alternative is using a filtering service. Roaring Penguin is a pretty decent one I have used in the past essentially you set your dns to send you mail to them first to get scanned then configure your filter service to send it to your real email server it the email passes the scans. This ensures that your server doesn't get blasted with spam and only the mail you get is legitimate.
